newsitem.title: USA: New England Power Pool asks users to conserve Wed..
newsitem.headline: New England Power Pool asks users to conserve Wed..

text.p: The New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) issued a request Tuesday for customers across the entire region to limit their use of electricity during peak demand hours Wednesday.
NEPOOL declared Wednesday a "conservation day" to reduce demand on the region's electrical energy supplies due to sustained hot and humid weather.
The pool projected power demand on its system to peak at 22,300 megawatts (MW) Wednesday with only 995 MW of generation on surplus reserve.
Energy conservation is also needed to comply with rules from state and federal environmental agencies, who are forecasting harmful air pollution levels in New England, NEPOOL said in a statement.
"We are asking them (customers) to keep the air more healthy," a Northeast Utilities spokesman said.
To meet a spike in power usage, utilities may activate 600 megawatts of generation from old power plants that emit more air pollutants than new, cleaner units, he said.
Through conservation measures, such as turning off unnecessary air conditioning, it becomes less necessary to fire up those older power plants, he said.
The conservation alert will end 2000 EDT Wednesday.
